How to verify a certificate

What comes with every certification, how to check that a document is genuine, and what you can share with a third party without handing over more than you need to.

Certificate holders Buyers and counterparties Audit and compliance
Before you
start

A certificate is three files, not one

All three say the same thing. They differ in who may see them, and in what each one carries printed on it.

For every certified document the platform keeps three versions and computes the digital fingerprint of each. Knowing which is which prevents the most common mistake: sending out the wrong one.

Stays on file

Original

The document exactly as it was filed, with no codes on it. It never leaves the platform: only internal staff can open it.

The authoritative one

Certified

The original with its barcode and QR stamped on. This is the file the certification refers to, and the holder's own copy.

This is the one you share

Distributable copy

Identical to look at, carrying an invisible watermark that lets it be recognised as a copy issued here even if it is renamed on the way.

The rule that matters

Send the third party the distributable copy. With it they can verify everything they need to verify. The certified copy you keep does not have to be handed over to prove anything.

Besides the files, every certification produces a twelve-character public code — the one you type to look the document up — and a certification record, a sealed file carrying the fingerprints of all three.

1Step

You go in through the firm's own site

Not through a link that arrives by email. The right door is one you type.

At propensionesabogados.com, open Platforms in the top menu and choose Certification. That link leads to the verification portal.

propensionesabogados.com→ Platforms→ Certification→ geausa.propensionesabogados.com/certificates/

Why we keep insisting on this

Always starting from the firm's own domain is what makes an impersonation fail: whoever builds a fake page can copy how the portal looks, but cannot put it under propensionesabogados.com. If an email carries a direct link, check that the domain is exactly geausa.propensionesabogados.com before typing anything.

2Step

Pick a portal: documents or people

It depends on what is in front of you: a piece of paper, or someone claiming to represent the firm.

3Step

A code to your email before you can look anything up

Only on the documents portal. The people portal does not ask for one.

The documents portal will not answer a stranger: it asks for an email address first and sends a six-digit code there. That is what stops someone from trying codes in bulk to find out which documents exist.

Confirm this before you walk a client through this step

By default the portal only accepts email from four corporate domains (propensionesabogados.com, bradbauhof.com, gyllton.com and recoveryrepatriationfoundation.com). A personal address gets «Only authorized emails». There is a setting — ALLOW_ANY_EMAIL_IPCON — that opens the portal to any address: check how it is set in production before telling a holder to come in here with their everyday email.

4Step

Two ways to check, and they are not equivalent

By code, or by uploading the file. The second answers a question the first one cannot.

Which one to use

If someone sends you a PDF and you want to know whether it is genuine, use method B. It is the only one that catches a document that looks right and reads wrong: a printed code can be copied off a photograph, but a file's fingerprint cannot be forged.

5Step

The result screen, read part by part

This is the screen an auditor will look at. It pays to know what each part is.

Without relying
on anyone

Check it yourself, with two commands

It works ten years from now, and it works even if the platform is down.

Everything above goes through the firm's website. An auditor will want something that does not, and that is what the certification record is for: a file holding the fingerprints of all three files with a cryptographic signature over it.

# 1. The fingerprint of the PDF you hold
sha256sum certificado.pdf                    # Linux or macOS
certutil -hashfile certificado.pdf SHA256   # Windows

# 2. Compare it against the record. If it matches one of the three,
#    the file is exactly the one that was registered.
files.original.sha256
files.certified.sha256
files.public_copy.sha256

The record also states the scope in writing — what it does and does not attest — along with the certification date and the canonical verification address. An extract, using this guide's demonstration data:

{
  "schema": "gea.certification-record/1",
  "status": "VALID",
  "issuer": { "name": "PROPENSIONES ABOGADOS INTERNACIONAL S.A.S.",
               "nit": "901.409.813-7" },
  "files": {
    "certified":   { "sha256":         "6069ea4899fbdf4438e037cd1b0bbbdf3e45362…",
                     "content_sha256": "71d7e786f06b4f06d2f6e73336b9046632ca87…" },
    "public_copy": { "sha256":         "2c1db40541c9ef4df52a0e07e24fd1e850554e…",
                     "content_sha256": "71d7e786f06b4f06d2f6e73336b9046632ca87…" }
  }
}

A detail that confuses people if nobody flags it

The content_sha256 of the certified file and of the distributable copy are the same, while their sha256 differ. That is deliberate: the content fingerprint ignores the watermark. It lets you prove that the copy in circulation says exactly what the certified original says, and still tell the two apart.

If there is
a summary

The AEGIS summary and a provable date

For when several documents are grouped, and for when you need to prove when.

An AEGIS summary is another document — with its own three files and its own certification — whose content is that it carries the codes of other documents printed on it. It does not contain them: it references them. Each grouped document gets its own code within the summary.

Why the QR does not carry the proof inside it

The printed QR points at that page, not at the block on the chain. If it carried the proof printed on it, the paper would have to be reissued every time the anchor advances. This way a single document is issued, and it does not go stale when the confirmation lands.

The other
portal

Checking the person, not the paper

For when someone says they are acting on behalf of the firm.

This portal is public: no email, no code. It accepts the four-character code on the credential, or the holder's document number.

The
limit

What exactly this attests

Saying it accurately protects everyone, starting with the firm.

It does attestIt does not attest
That the file you hold is byte for byte the one registered on the certification date.That what the document claims is true.
That any later alteration of the content is detectable.The existence, ownership or valuation of the assets it describes.
Who issued it, through the platform's signature over the record.That any third party has audited or accepted that content.
With a timestamp anchor, when that content existed, attested by a third party.Anything about what happened before that date.

When drafting emails and presentations

The record itself says so in writing, in a field called does_not_attest. Do not write copy that suggests otherwise: certification proves integrity and provenance, not truthfulness. Claiming more than you prove is what turns a defence into a problem.

Worth keeping
to hand

What to share, and what not to

What With a third party Why
Distributable copy (PDF)Share itThis is the version meant to circulate. It carries the invisible mark that lets it be recognised.
Public code, 12 charactersShare itIt is what the other side types to reach the document. It is printed on the PDF.
Certification record (JSON)Share itMade for an auditor. It does not contain the document, only its fingerprints.
Timestamp page linkShare itA public page. Fingerprints and dates only, no content.
Certified copy (your own, with the codes)Keep itNo need to hand it over: the distributable copy proves the same thing.
Original document, without codesNever leavesIt stays on file in the platform. Only internal staff can open it.
The six-digit code from your emailNeverIt is your session key: personal, single use. Nobody at the firm will ever ask you for it.

About the screenshots. All of them are of the real journey, taken against a demonstration environment with invented data: the company, the document, the codes and the person do not exist. No real certificate and no personal data of any kind appears. The boxes are drawn on each element's measured position, not estimated by eye.

One thing to confirm before handing this out. Step 3 depends on how ALLOW_ANY_EMAIL_IPCON is set in production. If it is closed, a holder with a personal email address cannot use the documents portal on their own and needs another route; worth confirming and adjusting that section accordingly.
